blocks.raw: <WikiExamTable headers={["Model/Approach","Theorist(s)","Year","Target Sclea or Radius","Key Principle"]} rows={[{"Model/Approach":"Garden City","Theorist(s)":"Ebenezer Howard","Year":"1898","Target Sclea or Radius":"30,000–60,000 people","Key Principle":"Self-sufficient new town combining city services with countryside amenities; community land ownership"},{"Model/Approach":"New Urbanism","Theorist(s)":"Duany, Plater-Zyberk, Calthorpe","Year":"1980s–present","Target Sclea or Radius":"400m (5-min walk)","Key Principle":"Walkable, mixed-use neighborhoods; all daily needs within walking distance; pedestrian-first design"},{"Model/Approach":"TOD","Theorist(s)":"Calthorpe et al.","Year":"1990s–present","Target Sclea or Radius":"400–800m from station","Key Principle":"Higher density, mixed-use development anchored to transit stations; reduced parking; active transport priority"},{"Model/Approach":"15-Minute City","Theorist(s)":"Carlos Moreno","Year":"2020","Target Sclea or Radius":"15 min walk/bike","Key Principle":"All daily needs (work, food, health, education, culture, parks) within 15-minute active transport radius"},{"Model/Approach":"CIAM / Athens Charter","Theorist(s)":"Le Corbusier, CIAM","Year":"1933","Target Sclea or Radius":"City-wide zoning","Key Principle":"Separation of four functions (living, working, recreation, transport) into distinct zones — OPPOSITE of mixed use"},{"Model/Approach":"Smart Growth","Theorist(s)":"Multiple practitioners","Year":"1990s–present","Target Sclea or Radius":"Urban-wide policy","Key Principle":"Compact infill, walkability, transit, mixed use, environmental conservation; anti-sprawl"}]} />

blocks.raw: <WikiMistakeList mistakes={["Confusing New Urbanism's 5-minute walk radius (400m) with TOD's catchment (400–800m)—the upper TOD bound is double the New Urbanism standard","Stating Garden City target population as 100,000 instead of 30,000–60,000—students often round up to memorable large numbers","Thinking CIAM advocated mixed use—CIAM advocated SEPARATION of functions; mixed use is a contemporary critique of CIAM's legacy","Attributing Garden City to Howard but not stating the correct target population range—Howard's vision is specific about sclea for a reason"]} />
